chapter: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
title: A new seven-piece band and learning to play on crutches
summary: Cobb forms a seven-piece band with Dickie Harris, Harold Cumberbatch and Eddie Lewis (nicknamed Tiger), and explains how he still needs crutches on steps.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: What sort of a band did you form now?
I had the same type of a band, seven pieces.
Seven pieces.
Baritone, trombone -- Dickie Harris was on the band, and I had Harold Cumberbatch back out of Brooklyn. Eddy Lewis was still with me on trumpet.
Hal who?
Huh?
Who was that --
Eddy Lewis, trumpet player I was telling you about.
Oh, yeah.
He was so meek and humble, we called him 'Tiger.'
And the same rhythm section?
'Tiger, how you doing?' 'Hi.'
(Laughter)
Well, Arnett, did you -- when you went back you just -- you had to use your crutches?

Oh, yeah, I've been on crutches ever since, and I will be on the rest of my life, but I'm doing much better. I'm on a level, I can walk without the crutches, as you see me doing now. But if I got to go down, a step down, a step up, I need them because, you know, I can't balance myself well.
Well, when you start --
Because I can't bend, you know.
Yeah. When you started off, you had to use them all the time, I guess, didn't you?
You mean after the accident?
Yeah.
I've been using them ever since the accident.
I mean could you walk on the level in the beginning? So you're making progress.

Yeah. Yeah, yeah. That's what I'm saying. I had to have them for everything. I couldn't move without them. You know, one thing I found out, that just a tip of a thing against the wall will balance you. I didn't know that until you have to go through the thing. It don't mean nothing, I mean just to stand. Just touch the wall, a tip, a small little thing will balance you. You don't need no whole grip, just touch.
